_copyLayers: Every 'name' and 'plain' field is Layer 1 — a non-technical, non-native English reader must understand it without help. 'alsoCalled' is Layer 2: it names the industry/AI term for the same thing so search and LLMs match it, while the human keeps reading plain words. Never move Layer 3 vocabulary into 'name' or 'plain'.
sectionIntro: Four ways to work together. Each one says what you receive and roughly how long it takes, so you know what you are buying before we talk.

firstStep.name: Scoping Week
firstStep.plain: A small paid first step, so neither of us has to guess. You explain the idea. I come back with a written plan: what gets built, what it does, in what order, how long each part takes, and what each part costs.
youReceive: A written plan you can hand to any developer — not only me
A list of every screen and feature, in order of importance
A timeline broken into stages, with a price for each stage
The main risks, and what I would do about them
firstStep.note: If you decide to build with me afterwards, this fee comes off the first stage. If you walk away, the plan is still yours to keep.

packages.name: First Working Version
packages.alsoCalled: MVP, minimum viable product, v1 launch
packages.plain: The first real version of your product — one that actual customers can use, not a demo. Phone app, website, and the server behind them.
youReceive: A phone app on the App Store and Google Play, or a website — or both
The server and database that run it
An admin screen so you can manage things yourself
It running live, for real users, not on my computer
packages.bestFor: You know what you want to build and you need it working and in front of people.

packages.name: Fix or Finish What You Have
packages.alsoCalled: project rescue, technical audit, handover, legacy takeover
packages.duration: 2–4 weeks to assess, then agreed per stage
packages.plain: Someone already started your product and it is late, broken, or slow — or the developer left. I read the existing work, tell you honestly what state it is in, and give you a plan to finish it.
youReceive: An honest written assessment of what exists and what it is worth keeping
A clear answer on repair versus rebuild, with the reasoning
A plan to finish it, priced by stage
I can do the work, or hand the plan to your own team
packages.bestFor: You have already paid for something that is not working, and you need to know where you stand.

packages.name: Make It Handle More Users
packages.alsoCalled: scaling, performance optimization, backend modernization, cloud migration
packages.plain: Your product works, but it is getting slow, expensive, or falling over as more people use it. I find what is causing it and fix it.
youReceive: A measured report of what is actually slow — not guesses
The fixes, applied and measured again afterwards
Lower running costs where the waste is in the setup
Monitoring, so you find out before your customers do
packages.bestFor: You already have customers and growth is starting to hurt.

pricing.title: How I price
pricing.body: I do not put one number on this page, because a fair price depends on what you actually need — and I would rather tell you the truth after looking than a number before. Here is exactly how it works.
points: We agree the work in stages. Each stage has its own fixed price, agreed before that stage starts.
You never get an open-ended bill. If a stage grows, we agree the change first.
You pay per stage, not everything upfront.
The code and the rights are yours from the first day, in your own account — not held by me.
The Scoping Week above is the cheapest way to find out what your project really costs.
